name: Fdg activation starts feeding
real_fly_result: Switching on the single pair of Fdg ('feeding') neurons makes a fly run its whole feeding sequence, proboscis extension included, with no food present.
model_test: Drive both Fdg neurons (50 and 100 Hz), no taste input. Read both MN9s, the model's proboscis-extension motor neurons.

numeric_target: none published in the abstract (direction only)
feasibility_reason: Fdg and MN9 are both in the brain model; one short activation run.
notes: Shiu et al. 2024 included Fdg among its 106 named SEZ types; check its figures so this exact comparison is not double counted.

name: One Fdg gives one-sided feeding
real_fly_result: Activating only one of the two Fdg neurons makes feeding movements lopsided, and killing one Fdg makes sugar-evoked feeding lopsided.
model_test: Drive the left Fdg alone, then the right Fdg alone. Compare left and right MN9.

mapping_confidence: high for the cells; moderate that a left/right MN9 difference is the right read-out
expected_model_result: The two MN9s respond unequally, and the stronger side flips when the other Fdg is driven.
feasibility_reason: The model can show a left/right MN9 difference, but 'lopsided feeding' is a proboscis movement that MN9 alone may not capture (other motor neurons, no body).

name: Fdg needed for sugar feeding
real_fly_result: Silencing or killing the Fdg neurons abolishes sugar-induced feeding, and Fdg respond to food only in starved flies.
model_test: The model's standard sugar input (21 sugar taste neurons, 100 Hz) with and without both Fdg silenced. Read MN9; also read Fdg itself during sugar input.
cell_types: stimulate: sugar taste neurons (model's standard set) [sim/shiu_model.py SUGAR_R_630] | silence: Fdg [Shiu et al. 2024 SEZ list (data/reference/sez_neurons.pickle, 'Fdg')] | read: MN9 (left, right) [sim/shiu_model.py] | read: Fdg [Shiu et al. 2024 SEZ list (data/reference/sez_neurons.pickle, 'Fdg')]
expected_model_result: Sugar-evoked MN9 falls to near zero with Fdg silenced.
feasibility_reason: Silencing is easy, but the model has no hunger state, and Shiu et al. 2022 found Fdg does not respond to taste on the proboscis (only to optogenetic sugar-neuron activation), so the fly's Fdg route may run through throat or leg sugar sensors the model lacks.
notes: May overlap the Shiu 2024 silencing screen if Fdg was in it; the real-fly comparison (Flood 2013) is the new part.

real_fly_result: Optogenetic activation of Usnea triggers proboscis extension, activation of G2N-1 or Clavicle increases it in food-deprived flies, activation of Fudog does not; hyperpolarising Rattle or Usnea reduces extension to 100 mM sucrose, while hyperpolarising other second-order neurons does not.

feasibility_reason: All cells and MN9 are in the model; each is one short run.
notes: The silencing half probably overlaps the already-covered Shiu 2024 silencing screen; the activation half may overlap Shiu 2024's own checks.

name: One dopamine neuron boosts sugar acceptance
real_fly_result: Activating dopamine neurons increases proboscis extension to sucrose (not to bitter or water), silencing them reduces it, and one SEZ dopamine neuron (TH-VUM) triggers extension and changes its activity with satiety.
model_test: Drive TH-VUM with weak sugar input; read MN9.
cell_types: stimulate: TH-VUM [Shiu et al. 2024 SEZ list (data/reference/sez_neurons.pickle, 'TH_VUM')] | read: MN9 [sim/shiu_model.py]
expected_model_result: Real fly: more extension to sugar.
feasibility_reason: The effect is dopamine modulation (slow). The published model treats dopamine as fast excitation, so a 'pass' would be for the wrong reason; with the Phase 7 slow-signal switch TH-VUM has no effect outside the mushroom body. Same problem the held-out lane found for OA-VPM4.
notes: Listed to show a clear model limit.

name: Courtship song reaches vpoEN
real_fly_result: The female's vpoEN neurons are auditory neurons tuned to specific features of the D. melanogaster courtship song, and they excite the vpoDN descending neurons that open the vaginal plates.
model_test: Drive the auditory Johnston's organ neurons (JO-A and JO-B) with pulse-song-like spike trains; read vpoEN and vpoDN.

expected_model_result: vpoEN fire; vpoDN follow.
feasibility_reason: Spikes can travel JO -> vpoEN, but song tuning depends on the timing pattern of sound and graded/active properties of antennal neurons; the model's JO input pattern would be made up.

name: Hearing neurons feed the giant fiber
real_fly_result: A subset of sound-detecting Johnston's organ neurons makes mixed electrical and chemical synapses onto the giant fiber (the escape neuron), and sound raises the chance that the giant fiber fires.
model_test: Drive JO-A/JO-B neurons, alone and together with a weak giant-fiber drive; read giant-fiber (DNp01) firing probability.

mapping_confidence: moderate (JO mapping); high for the giant fiber
expected_model_result: JO input raises giant-fiber firing probability.
feasibility_reason: The model has only the chemical half of this synapse; electrical synapses exist only as a Phase 7 switch in the antennal lobe.

name: Wind direction from both antennae
real_fly_result: Second-order mechanosensory neurons respond mainly to the same-side antenna, while 'wedge projection neurons' combine both antennae and give a more linear code for wind direction.
model_test: Drive left and right wind-sensitive JO neurons (JO-C/E) in different ratios; read second-order antennal-mechanosensory neurons and wedge projection neuron candidates.

expected_model_result: Read-out cells respond to the left-right difference.
feasibility_reason: Read-out cells unidentified; wind is a graded antenna displacement the model approximates with spike rates.

name: Head bristles aim grooming
real_fly_result: Each class of head bristle mechanosensory neuron, when activated, makes the fly groom the matching spot on its head; together they produce a whole-head grooming sequence.
model_test: None usable: the brain model could show which descending neurons each bristle class reaches, but the paper measured only behaviour, which is produced in the nerve cord.

name: Silenced glomerulus still gets lateral excitation
real_fly_result: When all sensory neurons of one glomerulus are genetically silenced, that glomerulus's projection neurons still respond to odours, because they receive substantial excitation from other glomeruli.
model_test: Silence the DA1 sensory neurons; drive many other sensory neuron types at odour-like rates (e.g. from the DoOR tables in data/olfaction/door); read DA1 projection neurons. Repeat with the al_ln_literature sign fix and the Phase 7 gap-junction switch.

expected_model_result: DA1 projection neurons fire above baseline despite silent DA1 input.
feasibility_reason: In flies much of this excitation travels through electrical synapses (excitatory local neurons coupled to projection neurons); the model has them only as the Phase 7 switch. The chemical part and the disputed local-neuron signs decide the published model's answer.
notes: A held-out SMELL test of the al_ln_literature fix (docs/heldout-validation.md asked for one); not covered by the olfaction lane. Reserve for the first batch.

name: Lateral inhibition scales with total input
real_fly_result: Inhibition between glomeruli outweighs excitation: removing input from other glomeruli broadens a projection neuron's odour tuning, and the inhibition grows with the total activity of all olfactory sensory neurons (divisive normalisation), acting partly on the sensory axon terminals.
source: Olsen & Wilson 2008, Nature 452:956 (PMC2824883); Olsen, Bhandawat & Wilson 2010, Neuron 66:287 (PMC2866644)
model_test: Drive the DA1 sensory neurons at a fixed rate (20, 40, 80 Hz) while adding more and more other sensory-neuron types; read DA1 projection neurons. Run the published model and the al_ln_literature sign fix.
cell_types: stimulate: DA1 sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type == 'ORN_DA1'] | stimulate: other olfactory sensory neurons [RULE: 630 hemibrain_type starting 'ORN_' except ORN_DA1, in growing subsets] | read: DA1 projection neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^DA1_[lv]PN$/]
root_ids_630: stimulate DA1 sensory neurons (n=126): see ids_630.csv | stimulate other olfactory sensory neurons: 630 hemibrain_type starting 'ORN_' except ORN_DA1, in growing subsets | read DA1 projection neurons (n=17): see ids_630.csv
expected_model_result: The DA1 projection-neuron response to the same DA1 input falls as total sensory activity rises (the curve shifts right).
feasibility_reason: Local-neuron synapses onto projection neurons and onto sensory terminals are in the connectome. Missing: the slow GABA-B part, which should weaken, not reverse, the effect.
notes: DUPLICATE: already being scored by the olfaction lane (docs/olfaction-vs-real-fly.md, items F3-F5, published model and al_ln_literature). Do not re-run here.

name: Projection neurons boost weak input
real_fly_result: Projection neurons amplify weak sensory input but not strong input (a saturating curve), respond more reliably from trial to trial than their sensory neurons, and emphasise odour onset.
model_test: Drive one glomerulus's sensory neurons (e.g. DA1) at 5-200 Hz; read its projection neurons; compare rates and trial-to-trial variability.

name: Sister projection neurons fire in sync
real_fly_result: Projection neurons fed by the same sensory-neuron type fire synchronised spontaneous spikes, odours make them more correlated, and projection neurons from different glomeruli are only weakly correlated.

name: APL keeps Kenyon cells sparse
real_fly_result: Kenyon cells excite the APL neuron and APL inhibits them; blocking this feedback makes Kenyon-cell odour responses less sparse and more alike between odours, and flies then fail to learn to tell similar odours apart.
model_test: Two similar odour-like inputs, with APL intact and silenced; read the fraction of Kenyon cells active and the overlap between the two odours' Kenyon-cell patterns.

expected_model_result: Silencing APL raises the active fraction and the overlap between odours.
numeric_target: baseline 5-10% of Kenyon cells respond to an odour (quoted in the paper); change: direction only
feasibility_reason: APL is a non-spiking neuron with local, graded inhibition; one LIF cell cannot do that. Kenyon-cell sparseness also depends on the Phase 7 threshold and sign fixes.
notes: DUPLICATE: already being scored by the olfaction lane (docs/olfaction-vs-real-fly.md, F7). Kenyon-cell sparseness itself was compared with Turner et al. 2008 in Phases 5 and 7.

real_fly_result: Optogenetically activating the GABAergic output neuron MVP2 (MBON-g1pedc>a/b) quickly and reversibly suppresses odour responses in the M4/6 output neurons, but has no visible effect on the V2a/V2a' output neurons.
model_test: Standard odour input to the mushroom body, with and without driving MBON11 (MVP2). Read M4/6 (MBON01, MBON02, MBON03, MBON04) and the V2 cluster (MBON18, MBON16, MBON17).

name: Learning shifts the M4b' odour response
real_fly_result: Aversive conditioning raises, and appetitive conditioning lowers, the M4b' output neuron's (MBON-b'2mp) response to the trained odour relative to the untrained one.
model_test: Phase 8: pair odour A with the punishment dopamine neuron PPL1-g1pedc (PPL101); test A and B; read MBON03/MBON04. Repeat with reward dopamine neurons of the b'2 compartments.

real_fly_result: Dopamine arriving after an odour (backward pairing) strengthens the Kenyon-cell-to-MBON-g4 synapse and raises the MBON's odour response, while forward pairing weakens it; one trial of the opposite order reverses either.
model_test: Phase 8 backward pairing; read the g4 output neurons.

notes: Also: Aso & Rubin 2016 (slow a3 learning) is NOT listed because Phase 8 already uses it to set SLOW_COMPARTMENTS, so it is not a fair test.

name: Looming detectors drive backward walking
real_fly_result: The visual projection neurons LC16 respond to looming and make flies walk backward, through the moonwalker descending neurons (MDN).
source: Sen et al. 2017, Curr Biol 27:766; Wu et al. 2016, eLife 5:e21022

feasibility_reason: LC16 and MDN both spike and are in the model; no eye is needed if LC16 is driven directly.
notes: Run SD2 in the same session (same cells).

real_fly_result: Turning while walking backward reflects unequal activation of the left and right MDNs; one-sided LC16 activation makes flies turn.
source: Sen et al. 2017, Curr Biol 27:766; Wu et al. 2016, eLife 5:e21022

name: Giant fiber adds looming size and speed
real_fly_result: The giant fiber sums two looming features: speed of expansion from LC4 and size from LPLC2. Silencing LPLC2 removes the size part of its response, leaving only the speed part; both synapse directly onto the giant fiber.
source: Ache et al. 2019, Curr Biol 29:1073; von Reyn et al. 2017, Neuron 94:1190
model_test: Drive LC4 and LPLC2 with loom-shaped rate time-courses; read the giant fiber; repeat with LPLC2 or LC4 silenced.
cell_types: stimulate: LC4 [630 hemibrain_type == 'LC4'] | stimulate: LPLC2 [630 hemibrain_type == 'LPLC2'] | read: giant fiber (DNp01) [630 cell_type == 'DNp01']

expected_model_result: Without LPLC2 the size-dependent part disappears; without LC4 the speed part does.

name: PFL3 steers through the lateral accessory lobe
real_fly_result: Optogenetically stimulating PFL3 neurons in the left or right lateral accessory lobe makes walking flies turn toward the stimulated side; about 8% of trials did not turn that way.
model_test: Drive the PFL3 neurons whose axons end in the left lateral accessory lobe (select by output side from the connection list); read DNa02 left vs right; then the right side.
cell_types: stimulate: PFL3 (split by output side before running) [630 hemibrain_type == 'PFL3'] | read: DNa02 (left, right) [630 hemibrain_type == 'DNa02']
root_ids_630: stimulate PFL3 (split by output side before running) (n=24): see ids_630.csv | read DNa02 (left, right) (n=2): 720575940604737708 720575940629327659
mapping_confidence: high for cells; the soma 'side' label is not the output side, so the split must be made from the wiring
expected_model_result: Left-side PFL3 drive gives more left than right DNa02 (a left turn by the body loop's rule), and the mirror for the right.
numeric_target: turn toward the stimulated side in about 92% of trials
feasibility_reason: PFL3 are spiking central-complex neurons with direct outputs in the lateral accessory lobe; the DNa02-to-turn rule is the body loop's existing assumption (Rayshubskiy et al. 2025).
notes: The model's known left lean in DNa02 (Phase 6) could bias this; run both sides and several seeds.

real_fly_result: MDN activity is needed for flies to walk backward at a dead end and is enough to make them walk backward.

name: Cool projection neurons follow cool sensors
real_fly_result: Projection neurons excited by cooling get mainly feed-forward excitation from cool-sensing receptor neurons.
model_test: Drive the cool sensory neurons (TRN_VP3a, TRN_VP3b); read the projection neurons of the VP3 glomerulus.
cell_types: stimulate: cool sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^TRN_VP3[ab]$/] | read: VP3 projection neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^(?:VP3\+_l2PN|VP3\+VP1l_ivPN|VP1l\+VP3_ilPN|VP3\+_vPN)$/]
mapping_confidence: high for the sensory neurons (FlyWire glomerulus labels); moderate-low for which FlyWire projection neuron is Liu's 'cool-PN'
expected_model_result: VP3 projection neurons fire.
feasibility_reason: Sensory and projection neurons spike and are in the model.
notes: Run in the same session as TH2 (first-batch rank 6).

name: Cool sensors inhibit warm projection neurons
real_fly_result: Warm projection neurons get excitation from warm receptors plus 'crossover' inhibition from cool receptors via local neurons: 14 of 17 recorded local neurons were tonically active, inhibited by warming and excited by cooling, and blocking inhibition depolarised warm projection neurons by 6 +/- 1 mV.
model_test: Drive the warm sensory neurons (TRN_VP2) at a fixed rate, with and without cool sensory drive (TRN_VP3a/b); read the VP2 projection neurons.
cell_types: stimulate: warm sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type == 'TRN_VP2'] | stimulate: cool sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^TRN_VP3[ab]$/] | read: VP2 projection neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^(?:VP2_adPN|VP2\+_adPN|VP2_l2PN)$/]
mapping_confidence: high for sensory neurons; moderate-low for the projection-neuron match
expected_model_result: VP2 projection neurons fire less when cool sensors are also active.
numeric_target: 14/17 local neurons cool-excited; +6 +/- 1 mV when inhibition is blocked
feasibility_reason: The sign depends on the model's local-neuron transmitters. The 'tonic' part needs baseline input, because the model's sensors are silent unless driven.

name: Cold projection neurons inhibit DN1a clock cells
real_fly_result: Cold-activated, GABAergic TPN-II projection neurons fire steadily below about 25 C and directly inhibit the DN1a clock neurons; picrotoxin (a GABA-A blocker) abolishes the cold inhibition.
model_test: Give DN1a a steady background input; add cool sensory drive (TRN_VP3a/b); read VP3+_vPN (the TPN-II candidate) and DN1a. Control: silence VP3+_vPN.
cell_types: stimulate: cool sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^TRN_VP3[ab]$/] | read: TPN-II candidate VP3+_vPN [630 hemibrain_type == 'VP3+_vPN'] | read: DN1a [630 hemibrain_type == 'DN1a']
mapping_confidence: moderate for TPN-II = VP3+_vPN (GABA-predicted in FlyWire, cold glomerulus, and Marin et al. 2020 say the slow-cool VP3 vPN targets the calyx micro-glomerulus that TPN-IIs innervate); high for DN1a
expected_model_result: VP3+_vPN fires; DN1a slows; the slowing disappears when VP3+_vPN is silenced.
feasibility_reason: All cells spike; one short run per condition.

name: Cooling excites DN1p clock cells
real_fly_result: DN1p clock neurons are excited by cooling and inhibited by heating, using thermoreceptors in the aristae and chordotonal organs.
model_test: Drive cool sensory neurons; read DN1pA/DN1pB. With a DN1p background input, drive warm sensory neurons and expect a drop.
cell_types: stimulate: cool sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^TRN_VP3[ab]$/] | stimulate: warm sensory neurons [630 hemibrain_type == 'TRN_VP2'] | read: DN1p [630 hemibrain_type matches /^DN1p[AB]$/]
mapping_confidence: moderate: FlyWire labels only part of the DN1p cluster
expected_model_result: Cool up, warm down.
feasibility_reason: The chordotonal-organ thermoreceptors are in the body (nerve cord), so part of the input is missing.

name: Humid-only and combined humidity-temperature projection neurons
real_fly_result: One projection neuron type samples only the humid-air glomerulus and responds only to humid air, while 'broadly tuned' projection neurons combine dry-air sensors with arista temperature receptors.
model_test: Drive humid (HRN_VP5), dry (HRN_VP4), warm (TRN_VP2) and cool (TRN_VP3a/b) sensors one at a time and in pairs; read all VP projection-neuron types.
cell_types: stimulate: humid sensors [630 hemibrain_type == 'HRN_VP5'] | stimulate: dry sensors [630 hemibrain_type == 'HRN_VP4'] | stimulate: warm sensors [630 hemibrain_type == 'TRN_VP2'] | stimulate: cool sensors [630 hemibrain_type matches /^TRN_VP3[ab]$/] | read: VP projection neurons [630 hemibrain_type matches /^VP\d/]
mapping_confidence: high for sensors; low-moderate for which FlyWire projection neurons match the paper's genetic lines

name: Song and mating-status inputs converge on vpoDN
real_fly_result: The female-only vpoDN descending neurons, which open the vaginal plates, get excitatory input from song-tuned vpoEN neurons and from pC1 neurons (which encode mating status); after mating, vpoDN's song responses drop but vpoEN's do not, via pC1.
model_test: Drive vpoEN; read vpoDN. Drive pC1 (all five subtypes); read vpoDN. Drive both together.
cell_types: stimulate: vpoEN [630 hemibrain_type == 'vpoEN'] | stimulate: pC1a-e [630 hemibrain_type matches /^pC1[a-e]$/] | read: vpoDN [630 hemibrain_type == 'vpoDN']
expected_model_result: vpoDN fires to each input and more to both together.
feasibility_reason: Small, fully labelled circuit; spiking cells.

name: SAG input picks out pC1a
real_fly_result: Activating the SAG ascending neurons (which carry the uterine sex-peptide signal) strongly depolarises pC1a, weakly depolarises pC1b, and has little or no effect on pC1c, pC1d and pC1e.
model_test: Drive the two SAG neurons (their axons are in the brain model); read pC1a to pC1e.
cell_types: stimulate: SAG [630 hemibrain_type == 'SAG'] | read: pC1a [630 hemibrain_type == 'pC1a'] | read: pC1b [630 hemibrain_type == 'pC1b'] | read: pC1c, pC1d, pC1e [630 hemibrain_type matches /^pC1[cde]$/]
expected_model_result: pC1a >> pC1b > pC1c/d/e (about zero).
numeric_target: rank order: pC1a strong, pC1b weak, pC1c-e little or none
feasibility_reason: Two input cells, ten read-out cells, one short run.

name: pC1 brakes egg laying through oviIN
real_fly_result: Photoactivating pC1 excites the GABAergic oviIN neurons, which inhibit the egg-laying descending neurons oviDN and their excitatory input oviEN (feed-forward inhibition).
model_test: Drive pC1; read oviIN. Give oviDN a background input, add pC1 drive; expect oviDN to drop; repeat with oviIN silenced.
cell_types: stimulate: pC1a-e [630 hemibrain_type matches /^pC1[a-e]$/] | read: oviIN [630 hemibrain_type == 'oviIN'] | read: oviDNa (FlyWire cell types oviDNa_a, oviDNa_b) [630 cell_type matches /^oviDNa_[ab]$/] | read: oviDNb [630 hemibrain_type == 'oviDNb'] | read: oviEN [NOT MAPPED: not labelled in FlyWire 630 or 783; use background drive instead]
expected_model_result: oviIN fires; oviDN slows; the slowing disappears with oviIN silenced.
feasibility_reason: All spiking, labelled cells.

name: pC1d/e leave minutes-long activity
real_fly_result: Brief activation of pC1d/e neurons produces persistent activity that lasts minutes in pC1 and aIPg neurons, supported by strong recurrent pC1d/e <-> aIPg wiring.
model_test: Drive pC1d and pC1e for 1-2 s, then stop; read pC1d/e and aIPg for at least 10 s afterwards.
cell_types: stimulate: pC1d, pC1e [630 hemibrain_type matches /^pC1[de]$/] | read: aIPg [783 hemibrain_type matches /^aIPg\d$/ (mapped to 630)]
mapping_confidence: high for pC1d/e; moderate for aIPg (FlyWire 783 labels mapped to 630)
expected_model_result: Real flies: activity outlasts the stimulus by minutes.
feasibility_reason: The model has no slow processes except adaptation, so any persistence must come from recurrent excitation; minutes-long persistence without runaway is unlikely. A strong test of the model's recurrent dynamics.

real_fly_result: T4 cells respond to moving bright edges and T5 cells to moving dark edges, each subtype tuned to one of four directions of motion.
